summary: This is a sound stage-5 correctness bisect step for the wgmma verify rewrite. Read against the s4 kernel, the Q A-fragment is the only per-segment input to tile lt>=1's S wgmma that differs from tile 0, and the S-vs-carry DIAG makes even a fallback run informative. Proceed with no companions, but fix how the reload is placed, and the lineage, before building.
justification: Mechanism (A). In s4's splitkv_verify_wgmma_kernel<TICKET,SYNC>, qa[2][4] is loaded only under `if (n == 0 || lt == 0)`, and the S wgmmas take it as the register A operand. The S accumulator is reset by scale_d=0 every tile. 1-tile segments pass at any ring stage, so the K descriptor/stage path and the V^T double buffer (n&1, which multi-request 1-tile runs also exercise) are already cleared, and SYNC rules out ring races. Between tile lt==0 and lt>=1 that leaves three differences: the qa reuse, the carried mA/lA/oacc, and the lt-dependent edge mask (lim). The rows go bad on all 128 rows, including unmasked ones, which points at S (qa) or the carry rather than the mask. The DIAG (tile-1 S vs the fp32 reference) separates those two in one check, so the run is interpretable whatever happens. Floors: verify_16 incumbent 162.8 us (FA3 main 151.6) against a 63.4 us floor, and verify_32 302.2 us (288.0) against 126.8 us. M2 (<=150 / <=280 us) only needs about 8% off the FA3 main kernel, a modest and physically reachable target for a single-pass FP8 wgmma kernel at ~2.4x above floor. Sliding and decode shapes are untouched, so flat is right. Weakest link (performance, not correctness): an unconditional per-tile reload 'from smem/L2' done as __ldg just before the S wgmma puts one L2 round trip (~0.5 us) on the critical path of EVERY tile. At ctx 80K, B=16 that is ~20K tiles over a 2*SM grid, ~75 tiles per CTA, i.e. tens of us exposed. That could erase the M2 margin and make the >=1.05x gate refuse a correct kernel. Stage Q in shared memory once per segment (ld.shared per tile), or issue the qa reload before wait_bar(full_bar(st)) so it overlaps the barrier wait. Root-causing also matters: a C++ register array held across iterations should not go stale. Dump SASS (cuobjdump -sass) and the ptxas wgmma-serialization warnings for qa's registers, so the fix is understood and not just worked around.
confounders: full-decode1-streamk-s3-two-level-ticket (master c3c1b01): the s4 branch lacks it (git merge-base confirms; s4's base table shows full decode_1 at 27.8 us vs master's 22.6 us). If s5 is built on s4 as written, the headline and full decode_1 will look worse than BEST from lineage alone, not from the verify change. The verify path is disjoint from the decode stream-K kernels, so rebase s5 onto master (frontmatter already says base: master) or judge strictly on the verify shapes' top_kernels.

fa3-hdim128-head-pairing / paired-heads-launch-cleanup (+ ab-tune-batch-gate): these define the incumbent being replaced at full verify_16/32 (paired FA3 + prepare + combine + paired norm-gate). The interleaved graph-replay gate must time exactly master's paired path, including _paired_norm_gate_kernel, or the >=1.05x routing decision is mis-anchored. That is not a confounder of the measured kernel's own time.

fused-preattention-triton: it writes the FP8 q (paired layout on full batched layers) that the new kernel reads via the qra/qrb addressing. If s5 sits on master, the q layout the kernel assumes (head-major, per-token HQ*D, unpadded vs paired-padded) must match what master's pre-attention kernel emits for the routed band. The self-check catches a mismatch, but it would show up as a fallback and be misread as the qfrag fix failing.
interference: No companions. This is a rewrite stage whose deliverable is the DIAG plus the self-check table; the next stage is the follow-up. A gain or loss on the headline is not the readout: verify_16/32 top_kernels against 151.6/288.0 us and the PATH CHOSEN lines are. The single-run ambiguities (S wrong vs carry wrong; correct-but-slower vs fallback) are already resolved inside the run by the DIAG and the printed paired timings. Attention has 8 checks left for 8 queued hypotheses, so an ab-revert or control would cost a check without adding information. The one lineage issue (s4 lacks c3c1b01) is fixed by rebasing, not by a companion run.
rules_flags: Module-global `_SPLITKV_GRID` (grid override set by the import-time self-check) must stay import-time only and never be mutated per call by kernel_fn (no per-call mutable Python state).

If Q is staged in smem per segment (recommended), it is read from the current call's q each segment. That is not caching derived from inputs; no global/static pointer to a state's q may persist across states (two-state rotation).
DIAG dumps and prints must live only in the prepare/self-check path. kernel_fn must stay print-free and sync-free, and the DIAG buffers must be shape/config-sized, never sized by seqlens.

FP8 P with Max_offset 8 (P = 2^(s - max + 8)) is FA3's own precision path, and softmax/merges stay fp32. That is within the q<=FP8/KV FP8/fp32 softmax bounds; confirm the coherent-data tolerance check runs on the routed band.
open_questions: Did s4's bisect include a 1-tile segment that STARTS mid-request (n == 0, lt >= 1, the stream-K tail case)? If it passed, the lt-based edge mask is cleared and qa is implicated even before s5's DIAG. If it was never tested, add it to the table.

Why would qa go stale at all? Does the SASS show ptxas reusing or rematerialising qa's registers across the loop (e.g. under register pressure with sacc/oacc/pa at 256 threads), and are there 'wgmma serialized' ptxas warnings? A real register-clobber root cause also threatens pa and the oacc carry.
After the fix, what are regs/thread and local bytes per variant? Reloading through smem keeps register pressure flat; an L2 __ldg reload before every tile adds latency on the critical path.
Will s5 be rebased onto master (c3c1b01) so that a promotable result carries master's full decode_1 stream-K kernel?
